slides.texte_overlay:
How to master the art of
small talk at work
Use the first and last five minutes of meetings. "How was your weekend?" while people arrive. These tiny moments build more workplace friendships than any team-building day.
Ask about their work, not just the weather. "What are you working on this week?" People enjoy talking about their projects, and you learn what's really happening in the company.
Be genuinely interested in other teams. "How does your team handle that?" Curiosity across departments makes you the guy everyone knows, which quietly helps your career.
Keep the elevator rule. Short, light, positive. "Busy day?" plus a smile is enough. Small talk at work is about warmth, not deep topics or complaining about the boss.
Remember personal details and follow up. "How did your daughter's football final go?" Coming back to something they told you weeks ago shows you care about people, not only tasks.
I do five minutes a day of history, art or science on my commute. At the coffee machine, I've always got something more interesting to share than the weather.

slides.texte_overlay: Stay away from gossip. When the chat turns to someone who isn't there, change the topic kindly. People trust and open up to the colleague who never talks badly about others.
